items.title: Live: Labor, Greens strike deal to cut self-managed super 'loophole' to pass tax changes
items.description: The Greens have announced they will support the federal government's capital gains tax budget measures through parliament. Follow live.

items.title: KPMG chair, audit partners to leave amid whistleblower fallout
items.description: KPMG chair Martin Sheppard and two audit partners are leaving the accounting and consulting giant in the wake of a scandal over misuse of confidential client information and the alleged mistreatment of a whistleblower.

items.title: Chemical regulator approves restricted use of controversial herbicide paraquat
items.description: The Australian Pesticides and Veterinary Medicines Authority concludes its nearly 30-year review of the controversial but popular herbicide.

items.title: Meet the 'King of the North' set to become the UK's new PM
items.description: A popular mayor but a virtual unknown on the global stage, Andy Burnham is poised to become Sir Keir Starmer's successor. Here's what that could look like.

items.title: Nose landing gear failure could have caused fatal plane crash, ATSB says
items.description: A plane crash that killed two people and injured several others in Adelaide earlier this year could have been caused by a failure in the plane's nose landing gear, an ongoing investigation has found.

items.title: Photo gives clues to missing man's final hours before disappearance
items.description: A previously unreleased image answers one question in the case of missing Queensland man Jack McLennan, but many others remain.

items.title: Live: Haaland, Mbappe and Messi make it another magic World Cup day
items.description: Kylian Mbappe and France put the foot down against Iraq after inclement weather forces a two-hour delay, while Erling Haaland nets again as Norway takes on Senegal. Follow live.

items.title: Perfect dupes of ABC articles are fuelling an industrial-scale scam
items.description: A $350 million scam is targeting Australians using AI-generated images of ABC journalists and politicians.

items.title: Ransom note claims Nancy Guthrie is dead, US media reports
items.description: CNN reported that one of the notes revealed that the mother of NBC's Today show host Savannah Guthrie was dead, and those who kidnapped her did not mean to kill her, but she died shortly after her disappearance.

items.title: Live: WiseTech executive chair Richard White denies human trafficking reports
items.description: WiseTech initially gained ground but is now in the red again after Monday's 18 per cent plunge. The ASX is seesawing between gains and losses. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Government responses criticised two months on from Kumanjayi Little Baby
items.description: Eight weeks on from the alleged murder of Kumanjayi Little Baby, Alice Springs community leaders are calling for an audit to determine why federal and territory government spending does not seem to be improving Indigenous living conditions and safety.

items.title: High cost of living fuels record regional migration, report says
items.description: The rate at which capital city dwellers are moving the regions is at its highest level on record, which the report's author says shows the trend is more than a post-COVID blip.

items.title: Toll cap cut, new hospitals and schools in NSW budget plans
items.description: NSW Treasurer Daniel Mookhey has tempered expectations of a return to surplus ahead of Tuesday's budget. Here's what has been promised so far.

items.title: Qatar gas complex explosion leaves at least 13 people dead
items.description: The Sunday night blast in Qatar's Ras Laffan gas processing facility is one of the deadliest events recorded in gas industry.

items.title: 'Like looking into a mirror': I met my siblings at the age of 35
items.description: Cheryl van Wageningen was shocked to receive a letter revealing that not only was she Indigenous, but she had a brother and a sister.

items.title: You won't see Hugh Jackman the same after The Death of Robin Hood
items.description: Plus Toy Story 5 trots out the same old games, Australian horror scores another winner and Colony uses zombies to ring the warning bell about AI.

items.title: This artist 'stole' the Rosetta Stone from the UK and took it home to Egypt
items.description: The Rosetta Stone changed the way we understood Ancient Egypt. It sits in the British Museum but this artist wanted to return it home. To pull it off he needed some legal advice, a digital scanner and the courage to take on the way we look at history.

items.title: Inspired by volcanoes, this new technology could affect billions of people
items.description: Private companies want to reflect the Sun to cool the planet. But scientists fear the geoengineering technology could disrupt monsoon rains a billion people depend on.

items.title: Security agencies issue blunt 'act swiftly' warning on AI
items.description: The Five Eyes agencies warn leaders must "act swiftly" to address the imminent threat as AI increases the "speed, scale and sophistication of cyber threats".

items.title: Australians have record-low trust in the United States, new poll finds
items.description: The Lowy Institute's latest poll shows Australia's trust in the US has fallen to a record low.

items.title: Potent sedative found in vapes sold in Melbourne
items.description: Victorian health authorities say vape products containing the powerful sedative etomidate have been found being sold illegally.

items.title: Music mogul Clive Davis dies at 94 leaving behind powerful imprint on industry
items.description: Clive Davis, the influential music industry mogul who fostered the careers of superstars such as Whitney Houston, Bruce Springsteen and Alicia Keys, has died. He was 94.

items.title: Union launches bid to save Boag's brewery from closure
items.description: The United Workers Union has launched a petition calling on Boag's parent company Lion Australia to sell rather than close its Launceston brewery. The union has also written to Premier Jeremy Rockliff urging him to intervene.

items.title: Victorian farm fined for not meeting free-range standards
items.description: Doreen Egg admits it sold eggs labelled as "free range" despite its hens not having access to an outdoor range, as required under Free Range Egg Labelling Information Standard.

items.title: The hidden dynamic that could undermine global stocks
items.description: As we plough on through the fourth consecutive year of global stock records and huge annual advances, it's not surprising that many pundits have begun to question just how much longer this boom can continue.
